title: Commentary
description: The current state of evolving debates around secularism in India are analysed, particularly in light of recent demands to remove the term from the Preamble of the Indian Constitution on the grounds of perceived civilisational incompatibility. Secularism today unfolds in the context of a growing body of decolonial critiques of the vestiges of Western colonial influence, on the one hand, and the continued electoral, political, and cultural predominance of ethnonationalist forces, on the other.
